findings.text: 经常基于同一套内部手册回答问题的团队，需要限定可搜索的资料范围，并把答复和可复核的原文线索一起交给审核者。[Q01](#research-q01)
独立服务按会话、知识目标及模型配置选择聊天或检索问答。检索阶段按模型空间聚合目标，按库授权后取回候选并有条件融合，再经重排、合并和筛选向模型提供材料，生成前可流出候选引用。[Q02](#research-q02) [Q03](#research-q03)
仅静态核查根产品的快速问答主路、混合检索和默认 Compose 下的文件导入边界。根仓 VERSION 声明 0.9.0，详情中的包版本未声明源自根目录没有 npm 包清单。DSH 连接器、Agent 任务执行、Wiki 以及具体后端的全量审计均不在本次抽读范围。
README.md:85–105 指向独立 Docker 或 Kubernetes 部署。VERSION 文件声明 0.9.0，Compose 未设 WEKNORA_VERSION 时可以引用 latest，实际镜像内容需要按环境核对。此根组件归类为基础设施。

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次使用 | 应用、数据库、队列、解析和索引算力 | 配置、清洗资料、授权及核对索引 | 环境和用时未知 |
| 持续使用 | 存储、嵌入和问答调用，按配置另计重排与追踪 | 更新资料、跟踪失败及核查关键引用 | 模型价格、调用量及负荷未测 |
| 失败恢复 | 重试、重建索引和备份空间 | 对照文件、任务及检索结果，核对哪些资料可用 | 入队失败可返回已保存记录，实际恢复时间未知 |
| 升级或退出 | 备份与迁移期间资源 | 演练还原或重建索引，保留手工查阅路径 | 迁移兼容和数据损失范围未测 |

以审核通过且能追溯原文的一次答复为单位，分别记录现金支出和人工时长。把失败、兜底、重试和复核计入总投入，并单列合格答复数与失败率。[Q04](#research-q04)
[Q05](#research-q05) 先取十几条含正例、无依据和越权哨兵的手册问题，关闭网络检索，确认模型和资料的权限边界。用固定兜底、原文复核和人工查阅基线比一轮，出现越权或关键事实无法溯源时暂停自动答复，保留原资料和人工审核。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 权限内取材 | 会话所有权和目标库访问各有服务端检查 | 实际跨租户、撤权和引用跳转一致性 |
| 给答疑提供出处 | 对有合并结果的问答发候选引用 | 引用是否覆盖每个关键判断 |
| 失败可区分 | 源码分别处理取消、异常、无结果和兜底 | 目标环境的错误率和误答比例 |
| 复用资料问答流程 | 索引、问答、引用输出已接线 | 相对人工流程能省多少操作和复核 |
[Q02](#research-q02) 可复用的是以知识库目标、向量空间和角色约束组织查询，再在流式生成前单独发候选引用。移植时须一起移交调用方身份、会话归属和库授权语义。单测和统计不提供真实可用性。根仓 inventory 统计 Markdown 和 JS/TS，分析重点是服务端 Go、配置及部署接线，Go 规模不纳入该表。
[Q01](#research-q01) 与 [Q02](#research-q02) 支持的贡献是把按知识库划定范围、混合检索、流式问答和复核资料组织成连续流程。归并知识库的权限与嵌入空间、提供回答前的引用事件，都是对索引和模型的组织工作。向量模型、关键词检索和排名融合算法本身已有独立来源。
[Q03](#research-q03) 自带配置允许在检索无结果后调用模型生成兜底答复，候选引用又在生成前发出。若把正常结束或出现引用当作答复有据的验收条件，就可能把没检索到支持材料的答案送入业务流程。按角色验证范围，逐条核对关键事实与引用原文。
[Q05](#research-q05) 把已有固定兜底策略和引用输出接入内部答疑复核流程。让无命中问题停止自动答复并转人工，正常回答先检查所引片段是否支持关键事实。若错误放行没有下降，或复核与转交增加的时间抵消改善，该假设不成立。

#### 启动与依赖

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 默认 Compose 的 App、Redis、PostgreSQL、docreader | 此部署路径需要 | 启动应用、持久化、排队及文档解析 | 先核对容器和健康检查，暂不导入资料 |
| Web 容器 | Web 试用需要 | 连接 App 的用户入口 | 可改为单独验收 API，不沿用 Web 体验结论 |
| 有检索能力的库及配套嵌入模型 | 向量问答需要 | 对资料和查询建立相容的向量表示 | 核对是否有关键词分支，保留无结果或错误 |
| 问答模型 | 生成需要 | 按上下文产生回复 | 保留检索和人工答复 |
| 重排模型 | 按配置选用 | 调整检索候选顺序 | 核对日志和实际排序，重排不可用时可走已有候选 |
| 授权角色与非敏感试用资料 | 本轮建议的业务前提 | 逐库约束访问并验证来源 | 出现越权或资料出站边界不明即停止试用 |

technical.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 排名融合和 RAG 本身已有先例，增量在候选、模型空间和多存储接线，技术新意按局部组合取四分之一。会话事件把可跳过、可失败的阶段串起，逐库授权后再进入存储和向量空间检查，机制有实质增量，未实测各存储组合。可复用的是带范围的检索和事件引用接口，迁移仍依赖知识库标识和调用方权限，迁移性取二分之一。组合已有入口让调用方少写接线，部署依赖仍多，简化取四分之一。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 和 [Q04](#research-q04) 相对共享目录人工搜查，同一知识库可持续接入答疑并给审核者候选出处，工作流和答复验收分别有实质变化，按二分之一取档。只对已有数字资料与部署人手的团队降低使用门槛，覆盖人群为小幅增量。索引与配置可复用，但带来存储、维护和复核负担，尚无单位成本数据，经济结构按小幅增量。

recommendation.reason: 已有资料管理员和自托管能力的团队可以用 WeKnora 对非敏感内部手册做问答试用。相比在共享目录逐份翻找，WeKnora 能把按知识库检索出的原文线索随回答交给审核者。如果读到未获授权的片段或关键结论找不到原文支持，就停止自动答复，退回受权限控制的文档检索和人工审核。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) README.md:43–49 说明反复利用团队资料的目标，会话服务在生成前发候选引用，使角色、现有搜文件流程和有出处答复的验收目标都可落地，高于偶发便利档。缺真实团队的问答频次、查错版本及排障代价，未达较充分的重复摩擦证据。

advantage.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) [Q02](#research-q02) session_knowledge_qa.go:725–732、1306–1319 支持把可查资料线索交给审核者，检索与回答有实际连接，高于单入口包装。候选列表先于回答，且 Q03 的无命中模型兜底仍可输出，关键结论的证据覆盖和与人工方案的质量比较不明，暂不取较充分档。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) [Q03](#research-q03) routes_chat.go:145–162、session_knowledge_qa.go:190–233、768–795、知识库服务逐库权限源码覆盖入口、调用、依赖与主要失败路径，超过局部线索档，可支撑隔离试用。没有真实数据库、模型或跨角色故障实测，达不到本地执行档。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04) [Q05](#research-q05) docker-compose.yml:409–415 和 knowledge_create.go:272–293 显示接入要维护多服务及异步导入。对保留原资料且已有运维人员的非敏感试用，有查状态、以已知问题复核、回到原文的退路，高于重要退路缺失档。数据库恢复、模型支出和日常复核仍需人工且未量化，达不到负担较轻档。

publication.summaries.text: 面向团队文档的知识服务，提供检索问答、Agent 推理和 Wiki 管理。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 独立知识检索 | 按库和文档范围找候选片段 | 需要实际授权和可检索索引 |
| 流式知识问答 | 在同一会话获取回复和检索引用 | 需要问答模型，是否检索取决于范围和配置 |
| 候选重排 | 过滤或调整检索片段顺序 | 无重排模型或请求失败时可继续使用已有候选 |
| 异步文件导入 | 上传文件并安排后台切块、索引 | 返回文件记录后仍要检查处理状态 |

publication.advice.text: [Q05](#research-q05) 先取十几条含正例、无依据和越权哨兵的手册问题，关闭网络检索，确认模型和资料的权限边界。用固定兜底、原文复核和人工查阅基线比一轮，出现越权或关键事实无法溯源时暂停自动答复，保留原资料和人工审核。

\n\n## Overview\n\n[WeKnora](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com) is an open-source, LLM-powered knowledge framework for enterprise document understanding, semantic retrieval and reasoning. It brings a team's documents together so they can be searched, reasoned over and kept up to date.\n\nhttps://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de0e490a-e738-405e-bb3a-64b63edd7278\n\n

v0.9.0 · 2:45 · 1080p60 · English narration and subtitles

\n\nUse RAG to look things up, the agent for multi-step tasks, and the wiki to organize knowledge. All three work on the same knowledge bases.\n\n\n \n \n\n\n**The agent's toolbox.** Skills installed from ClawHub / SkillHub / Git / ZIP run in session-persistent Docker / E2B / Cube sandboxes, with an interactive terminal and graphical desktop beside the chat. Through the BrowserSkill extension the agent operates the user's own Chrome or Edge, and external MCP services (OAuth included) can be connected and enabled tool by tool.\n\nBeyond the three modes:\n\n- **Memory and curation**: cross-session long-term memory keeps the profile, preferences and facts a user has confirmed. Folder uploads keep their directory tree, and retrieval chunks can be edited, diffed and rolled back.\n- **Data sources and formats**: auto-sync from Feishu wiki / Feishu Drive / Confluence / GitLab / Tencent IMA / Notion / Yuque / DingTalk Docs / Seafile / RSS, with more on the way. 10+ document formats including PDF, Word, images, Excel and XMind; Office files are parsed in-process by anydoc.\n- **Channels and integrations**: Q&A in WeCom, Feishu, Slack, Telegram and other IM apps; an embed widget for external websites; a built-in MCP Server for Cursor, Claude and other AI tools; scoped API keys with a principal model for programmatic access.\n- **Models**: 29 built-in vendors with a generated model catalog, including OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen (Alibaba Cloud), Zhipu, Hunyuan, Gemini, MiniMax, NVIDIA, LiteLLM and Ollama.\n- **Permissions and operations**: multi-workspace RBAC (four roles, per-resource ownership, per-workspace audit log), several storage instances per workspace, a runtime task-queue dashboard with worker-pool governance, and Langfuse tracing for agent steps, token usage and pipelines.\n- **Deployment**: LLMs, vector databases and storage backends are all swappable. Deploy locally or on a private cloud and keep the data in your own environment.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n\n \n \n \n \n \n

\n\n### Run with Docker Compose\n\nRequires [Docker](https://www.docker.com/), [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/) and [Git](https://git-scm.com/).\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora.git\ncd WeKnora\ncp .env.example .env # Edit .env as needed, see comments in the file\ndocker compose pull # Pull the latest images\ndocker compose up -d # Start core services\n```\n\nThen open **http://localhost** and follow the onboarding guide. A walkthrough with sample data is in the [Quickstart](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/03-quickstart).\n\n> [!TIP]\n> To use a local Ollama model, run `ollama serve > /dev/null 2>&1 &` first. For the Ollama embedding model name, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, and RAM notes, see [Configuration](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/04-configuration).\n\n| Service | URL |\n|---------|-----|\n| Web UI | `http://localhost` |\n| Backend API | `http://localhost:8080` |\n| Langfuse Tracing | `http://localhost:3000` |\n\n### Optional services\n\nAdd `--profile` flags to enable additional components; multiple profiles can be combined.\n\n| Profile | Adds |\n|---------|------|\n| _(default)_ | Core services |\n| `full` | All features |\n| `neo4j` | Knowledge Graph (Neo4j) |\n| `minio` | Object Storage (MinIO) |\n| `langfuse` | Tracing (Langfuse) |\n\n```bash\ndocker compose --profile neo4j --profile minio pull\ndocker compose --profile neo4j --profile minio up -d\ndocker compose down # Stop services\n```\n\n### Upgrading\n\nIf you already have WeKnora running and downloaded a newer release:\n\n```bash\n# Set WEKNORA_VERSION in .env to the target release (e.g. 0.9.0), or keep latest\ndocker compose pull # Pull images matching WEKNORA_VERSION\ndocker compose up -d # Recreate containers with new images\n```\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> `docker compose up -d` alone reuses locally cached images and may leave the UI version out of sync with the release you downloaded. Read the [upgrade notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#upgrade-notes) before upgrading. Deployments older than v0.8.2 should also read the [v0.8.2 notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#upgrade-notes).\n\n### Other ways to deploy\n\n| Option | When to use it |\n|--------|----------------|\n| **Docker Compose** | The standard deployment above: all features, multiple services |\n| **Kubernetes (Helm)** | Production clusters; the chart is in [`helm/`](./helm) |\n| **Lite single binary** | Local or low-resource use with no external dependencies (SQLite + in-memory queue); see [Lite vs. standard](./docs/LITE.md) |\n| **Desktop app** | The Lite runtime with a GUI, login-free start and a macOS host sandbox; no installer is published yet, so build it from source |\n\nAll options, hardware requirements and deployment topologies: [Installation guide](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/02-installation).\n\n> [!WARNING]\n> WeKnora ships with login authentication, but for production deployments we strongly \n\n## Product Tour\n\n### Quick Q&A and smart reasoning\n\n**Two ways to ask.** Quick Q&A answers from the knowledge base with RAG and cites the sources it used. In smart reasoning the agent plans multi-step work, searching, reading documents and calling tools and skills, and shows each step in the conversation. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/18-chat-experience)\n\n\n\n \n \n\n\n\n### Local browser\n\n**Operate the browser on your computer.** Through Tencent's open-source BrowserSkill extension, the agent opens pages and fills in forms in your own Chrome or Edge, and hands over to you for logins and CAPTCHAs. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/05-clients/09-local-browser)\n\n\n\n \n \n\n\n\n### Skills and sandbox\n\n**Run skills and produce files.** Docker, E2B and Cube backends are supported. Turns in the same session share one workspace, and generated files can be previewed and downloaded. Open the graphical desktop or interactive terminal beside the chat to follow each step and take over when needed. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/22-skills-sandbox)\n\n\n\n \n \n\n\n\n### Toolbox: MCP services and skills\n\n**Tools the agent can use.** Connect external MCP services and choose, tool by tool, which are enabled and which calls need approval. Install skills from ClawHub, SkillHub, Git or ZIP, manage them per workspace, and reuse them across sandboxes. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/22-skills-sandbox)\n\n\n\n \n \n\n\n\n### Automatic wiki\n\n**Documents organized into a browsable wiki.** With Wiki enabled, WeKnora extracts people, products and concepts from knowledge-base documents into pages with source citations, organized by directory. The knowledge graph shows how pages relate; pages can be edited directly and every change can be rolled back. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/14-wiki)\n\n\n\n \n \n\n\n\n### Observability\n\n**Tracing and runtime monitoring.** Langfuse traces the reasoning, tool calls and token usage of each agent step. The document parsing timeline shows progress stage by stage, and the task-queue dashboard lists queued and failed tasks. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/16-observability)\n\n\n\n \n \n\n\n\n## Architecture\n\n\n\n \n \n\n\n\nA modular pipeline from document parsing, vectorization and retrieval to LLM inference, in which every component can be replaced or extended. Each RetrieveResult stays its own list: they come from\n// different engines, store groups and parameter sets (document vs FAQ), are\n// appended in goroutine completion order, and their positions are only\n// meaningful within the list.\nfunc classifyRetrievalResults(ctx context.Context, retrieveResults []*types.RetrieveResult) (\n\tvectorLists, keywordLists [][]*types.IndexWithScore,\n) {\n\tfor _, retrieveResult := range retrieveResults {\n\t\tlogger.Infof(ctx, \"Retrieval results, engine: %v, retriever: %v, count: %v\",\n\t\t\tretrieveResult.RetrieverEngineType,\n\t\t\tretrieveResult.RetrieverType,\n\t\t\tlen(retrieveResult.Results),\n\t\t)\n\t\tif len(retrieveResult.Results) == 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif retrieveResult.RetrieverType == types.VectorRetrieverType {\n\t\t\tvectorLists = append(vectorLists, retrieveResult.Results)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tkeywordLists = append(keywordLists, retrieveResult.Results)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn\n}\n\n// flattenLists concatenates retrieval lists.\nfunc flattenLists(lists [][]*types.IndexWithScore) []*types.IndexWithScore {\n\tvar out []*types.IndexWithScore\n\tfor _, list := range lists {\n\t\tout = append(out, list...)\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// fuseOrDeduplicate either fuses vector+keyword results via RRF or deduplicates\n// single-retriever results. Raw BM25\n\t\t// (often >10) saturates compositeScore's 0.3*base term. BM25 from\n\t\t// different engines or indexes is not comparable, so each list is\n\t\t// scaled by its own best score.\n\t\tfor _, list := range keywordLists {\n\t\t\trescaleUnboundedScores(list)\n\t\t}\n\t\tresult := deduplicateByScore(flattenLists(keywordLists))\n\t\tlogger.Infof(ctx, \"Result count after deduplication: %d\", len(result))\n\t\treturn result\n\t}\n\t// Hybrid: use RRF fusion to merge vector + keyword results\n\tresult := fuseWithRRF(ctx, vectorLists, keywordLists, retrievalCfg)\n\tlogger.Infof(ctx, \"Result count after RRF fusion: %d\", len(result))\n\treturn result\n}\n\n// sortByScoreDesc orders hits by descending score, then chunk ID to keep tied ranks stable.\nfunc sortByScoreDesc(a, b *types.IndexWithScore) int {\n\tif a.Score > b.Score {\n\t\treturn -1\n\t} else if a.Score < b.Score {\n\t\treturn 1\n\t}\n\treturn cmp.Compare(a.ChunkID, b.ChunkID)\n}\n\n// deduplicateByScore deduplicates retrieval results by chunk ID, keeping the highest score\n// for each chunk. Returns the results sorted by score descending.\n// Used when only a single retriever (e.g. vector-only for FAQ) is active.\nfunc deduplicateByScore(results []*types.IndexWithScore) []*types.IndexWithScore {\n\tchunkInfoMap := make(map[string]*types.IndexWithScore, len(results))\n\tfor _, r := range results {\n\t\tif existing, exists := chunkInfoMap[r.ChunkID]; !exists || r.Score > existing.Score {\n\t\t\tchunkInfoMap[r.ChunkID] = r\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tdeduped := make([]*types.IndexWithScore, 0, len(chunkInfoMap))\n\tfor _, info := range chunkInfoMap {\n\t\tdeduped = append(deduped, info)\n\t}\n\tslices.SortFunc(deduped, sortByScoreDesc)\n\treturn deduped\n}\n\n// rescaleUnboundedScores maps a single-retriever candidate set onto [0, 1]\n// by dividing through the maximum finite score. Keyword (BM25) scores are\n// unbounded; leaving them in place saturates compositeScore (0.3*base with\n// a [0, 1] clamp) so every candidate ties at 1.0 and MMR degenerates to\n// diversity-only ordering.\n//\n// Scores already in [0, 1] are left unchanged so engines that stamp\n// keyword hits at 1.0 (Qdrant, Doris) and already-normalized vector\n// scores keep their current magnitude. Relative order is preserved\n// either way. Retrieve/Langfuse sampling happens before fusion, so\n// raw BM25 remains visible in the retrieve span.\nfunc rescaleUnboundedScores(results []*types.IndexWithScore) {\n\tmaxScore := 0.0\n\tfor _, r := range results {\n\t\tif r == nil {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif math.IsNaN(r.Score) || math.IsInf(r.Score, 0) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif r.Score > maxScore {\n\t\t\tmaxScore = r.Score\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif maxScore <= 1 {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tfor _, r := range results {\n\t\tif r == nil {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase math.IsNaN(r.Score), math.IsInf(r.Score, -1), r.Score <= 0:\n\t\t\tr.Score = 0\n\t\tcase math.IsInf(r.Score, 1):\n\t\t\tr.Score = 1\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tr.Score = r.Score / maxScore\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// fuseWithRRF merges vector and keyword retrieval results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion.\n// RRF score = vectorWeight/(k+vectorRank) + keywordWeight/(k+keywordRank),\n// divided by its maximum (vectorWeight+keywordWeight)/(k+1) so it lands in\n// [0, 1] like the single-retriever paths. !exists || r.Score > existing.Score {\n\t\t\tchunkInfoMap[r.ChunkID] = r\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor _, r := range flattenLists(keywordLists) {\n\t\tif _, exists := chunkInfoMap[r.ChunkID]; !exists {\n\t\t\tchunkInfoMap[r.ChunkID] = r\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Compute weighted RRF scores and assign to each chunk\n\tresult := make([]*types.IndexWithScore, 0, len(chunkInfoMap))\n\tfor chunkID, info := range chunkInfoMap {\n\t\trrfScore := 0.0\n\t\tif rank, ok := vectorRanks[chunkID]; ok {\n\t\t\trrfScore += vectorWeight / float64(rrfK+rank)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif rank, ok := keywordRanks[chunkID]; ok {\n\t\t\trrfScore += keywordWeight / float64(rrfK+rank)\n\t\t}\n\t\tinfo.Score = rrfScore / maxRRF\n\t\tresult = append(result, info)\n\t}\n\tslices.SortFunc(result, sortByScoreDesc)\n\n\t// Log top results for debugging\n\tfor i, chunk := range result {\n\t\tif i >= 15 {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tvRank, vOk := vectorRanks[chunk.ChunkID]\n\t\tkRank, kOk := keywordRanks[chunk.ChunkID]\n\t\tlogger.Debugf(ctx, \"RRF rank %d: chunk_id=%s, rrf_score=%.6f, vector_rank=%v(%v), keyword_rank=%v(%v)\",\n\t\t\ti, chunk.ChunkID, chunk.Score, vRank, vOk, kRank, kOk)\n\t}\n\n\treturn result\n}\n\n// bestRanks returns each chunk's best 1-based rank across lists, ranking every\n// list on its own by score (a chunk repeated in a list keeps its best score).\nfunc bestRanks(lists [][]*types.IndexWithScore) map[string]int {\n\tranks := make(map[string]int)\n\tfor _, list := range lists {\n\t\tfor i, r := range deduplicateByScore(list) {\n\t\t\tif current, ok := ranks[r.ChunkID]; !ok || i+1 < current {\n\t\t\t\tranks[r.ChunkID] = i + 1\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn ranks\n}\n" }, { "path": "internal/application/service/chat_pipeline/rerank.go", "content": "package chatpipeline\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\n\t\"github.com/Tencent/WeKnora/internal/reranking\"\n\t\"github.com/Tencent/WeKnora/internal/tracing/langfuse\"\n\t\"github.com/Tencent/WeKnora/internal/types\"\n\t\"github.com/Tencent/WeKnora/internal/types/interfaces\"\n)\n\n// PluginRerank implements reranking functionality for chat pipeline\ntype PluginRerank struct {\n\tmodelService interfaces.ModelService // Service to access rerank models\n\t// kbService reads the images of image hits for a reranker that scores\n\t// images. {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcloseThinking()\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t\tif response.ResponseType == types.ResponseTypeAnswer {\n\t\t\t\t\t// Providers can emit a completion once for Resolution is sequential and can rebuild a\n// missing engine, so the worst case is one build timeout per distinct store;\n// this bounds the total rather than the individual attempt.\nconst storeResolveBudget = 12 * time.Second\n\n// storeGroup is one fan-out unit of HybridSearch: a set of KB IDs that share\n// the same (VectorStore, owning tenant) pair.\n//\n// Partition key is (VectorStoreID, OwnerTenantID), not VectorStoreID alone,\n// because Organization-shared KBs (kb.TenantID != requestTenantID) need\n// their own group whose ownership lookup runs against kb.TenantID — the\n// store is owned by the source tenant, not the caller.\n//\n// BaseParams are immutable across iterations and goroutines. TopK is the\n// only mutable per-iteration value; paramsWithTopK builds a fresh\n// []RetrieveParams per call so no goroutine sees a slice being mutated by\n// another. Callers MUST NOT mutate BaseParams after resolveStoreGroups\n// returns; doing so would race with the fan-out goroutines.\ntype storeGroup struct {\n\t// StoreID is the bound VectorStore UUID, or \"\" for the env-store group\n\t// (KBs with VectorStoreID = NULL). Never echo this in user-facing\n\t// errors; use secutils.SanitizeForLog when emitting in structured logs.\n\tStoreID string\n\n\t// OwnerTenantID is the tenant that owns the KBs and the store for this\n\t// group. For Organization-shared KBs this differs from the request's\n\t// tenant; the factory's StoreOwnedBy must be called with this value.\n\tOwnerTenantID uint64\n\n\t// KBIDs are the knowledge base IDs in this group. The caller MUST have\n\t// authorized the request to access every ID here (the trust boundary\n\t// is the HTTP handler / session layer, matching the pre-existing\n\t// chat_pipeline pattern).\n\tKBIDs []string\n\n\t// Engine is the resolved CompositeRetrieveEngine for this group.\n\t// Reused across iterative FAQ retries — never re-resolved.\n\tEngine *retriever.CompositeRetrieveEngine\n\n\t// BaseParams is the immutable per-group retrieval parameter list.\n\t// TopK is filled in at retrieve time via paramsWithTopK.\n\tBaseParams []types.RetrieveParams\n\n\t// TopK is the requested over-retrieval count. The iterative FAQ path\n\t// (knowledgebase_search_faq.go) updates this between calls to\n\t// retrieveFromStores. Single-shot HybridSearch sets it once.\n\tTopK int\n\n\t// ImageKBIDs are the KBs of this group whose image vectors the search\n\t// recalls: they opted in (KnowledgeBase.IsImageVectorEnabled) and the\n\t// embedding model embeds images. When it is non-empty the group's\n\t// document vector search is widened to find image rows, and\n\t// VectorThreshold is the text threshold, which filterImageHits restores\n\t// on text hits. Image hits of any other KB are dropped.\n\tImageKBIDs map[string]struct{}\n\tVectorThreshold float64\n}\n\n// imageRecall reports whether any KB of the group recalls image vectors.\nfunc (g *storeGroup) imageRecall() bool {\n\treturn len(g.ImageKBIDs) > 0\n}\n\n// resolveStoreGroups partitions kbs by (VectorStoreID, KB.TenantID),\n// resolves the engine per group via the PR2 factory using the OWNING\n// tenant for ownership lookup, and builds the per-store base RetrieveParams\n// once. Returns groups in non-deterministic order (caller must not rely on\n// iteration order).\n//\n// The primary KB supplies the embedding model and FAQ type for params; the\n// caller MUST invoke validateSameEmbeddingModel first to guarantee a\n// single embedding model identity across kbs.\n//\n// Errors are translated from sentinel to typed AppError so that the\n// upstream handler reports a stable error code without leaking storeIDs:\n//\n// - retriever.ErrVectorStoreForbidden →\n// apperrors.NewVectorStoreBindingInvalidError (2200)\n// - retriever.ErrVectorStoreNotFound →\n// apperrors.NewVectorStoreUnavailableError (2201)\n// - retriever.ErrTenantInfoMissing →\n// apperrors.NewVectorStoreBindingInvalidError (2200)\n// - any other error → returned with %w wrap (no UUID embedded).\nfunc (s *knowledgeBaseService) resolveStoreGroups(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tprimary *types.KnowledgeBase,\n\tkbs []*types.KnowledgeBase,\n\tparams types.SearchParams,\n\tmatchCount int,\n) ([]*storeGroup, error) {\n\ttype partitionKey struct {\n\t\tstoreID string\n\t\ttenantID uint64\n\t}\n\tbuckets := make(map[partitionKey][]*types.KnowledgeBase)\n\tfor _, kb := range kbs {\n\t\tsid := \"\"\n\t\tif kb.HasVectorStore() {\n\t\t\tsid = *kb.VectorStoreID\n\t\t}\n\t\tkey := partitionKey{storeID: sid, tenantID: kb.TenantID}\n\t\tbuckets[key] = append(buckets[key], kb)\n\t}\n\n\t// Resolving a group can rebuild a missing store engine, which dials a\n\t// backend. Those rebuilds happen one after another here, and this server\n\t// sets no read or write timeout, so a search across several cold stores\n\t// would otherwise have nothing bounding it.
